questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In fungi, the body consists of long, slender, thread-like structures called hyphae. The network of hyphae is known as:

solution.explanation: With the exception of yeasts, which are unicellular, fungi are filamentous. Their bodies consist of long, slender, thread-like structures called hyphae, and the network of hyphae is known as mycelium.
solution.why_others_wrong: A conidiophore is the special mycelium on which conidia are produced. Basidiocarps and ascocarps are fruiting bodies of basidiomycetes and ascomycetes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi
solution.final_answer: Option B: mycelium

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT credits chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria with playing a great role in:

options.text: producing methane (biogas) from the dung of ruminant animals
recycling nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, iron and sulphur
fixing atmospheric nitrogen in specialised cells called heterocysts

solution.explanation: Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria oxidise various inorganic substances such as nitrates, nitrites and ammonia and use the released energy for their ATP production. They play a great role in recycling nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, iron and sulphur.
steps: Chemosynthetic bacteria: energy from oxidising inorganic substances
Role: recycling of N, P, Fe and S
solution.why_others_wrong: Methane is produced by methanogens (archaebacteria). Heterocysts are found in cyanobacteria such as Nostoc and Anabaena. Curd is made by heterotrophic bacteria.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Monera (eubacteria)
solution.final_answer: Option B: recycling nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, iron and sulphur

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Plants respond to external factors such as light, water, temperature, other organisms and pollutants.
Statement II: If increase in body mass is taken as the criterion for growth, non-living objects cannot be said to grow.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Response to stimuli; growth as a criterion
solution.explanation: All organisms can sense and respond to environmental cues; plants respond to external factors like light, water, temperature, other organisms and pollutants. NCERT points out that non-living objects also grow if increase in body mass is taken as the criterion: mountains, boulders and sand mounds grow, though by accumulation of material on the surface.
steps: Statement II: false; by the body-mass criterion, non-living objects also grow
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Diversity in the Living World (characteristics of living organisms)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, members of kingdom Animalia store their food reserves as:

solution.explanation: Members of Animalia are heterotrophic, eukaryotic, multicellular organisms whose cells lack cell walls. They directly or indirectly depend on plants for food, digest their food in an internal cavity and store food reserves as glycogen or fat.
solution.why_others_wrong: Starch is the food reserve of plants. Cellulose is a plant cell-wall material and chitin is found in fungal cell walls; neither is the stored food of animals.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Animalia
solution.final_answer: Option D: glycogen or fat

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (fungus) with List-II (kind of sexual spore).

List-I:
A. Rhizopus
B. Claviceps
C. Puccinia
D. Alternaria

List-II:
I. Basidiospores
II. Sexual stage not known
III. Zygospores
IV. Ascospores

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Classes of fungi and their sexual spores
solution.explanation: Rhizopus (the bread mould) is a phycomycete, in which a zygospore is formed by the fusion of two gametes. Claviceps is an ascomycete; its sexual spores, ascospores, are produced endogenously in asci. Puccinia (wheat rust) is a basidiomycete, which forms basidiospores on the basidium. Alternaria is a deuteromycete, a group in which only the asexual or vegetative phases are known.
steps: Alternaria: deuteromycete -> no known sexual stage

solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi (Phycomycetes, Ascomycetes, Basidiomycetes, Deuteromycetes)
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about archaebacteria are correct?

(a) They differ from other bacteria in having a different cell wall structure.
(b) Methanogens among them are present in the guts of several ruminant animals such as cows and buffaloes.
(c) The halophiles among them live in hot springs.
(d) The cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) belong to this group.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Archaebacteria live in some of the harshest habitats: extreme salty areas (halophiles), hot springs (thermoacidophiles) and marshy areas (methanogens). They differ from other bacteria in having a different cell wall structure, which is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions. Methanogens are present in the guts of several ruminant animals such as cows and buffaloes and are responsible for the production of methane (biogas) from their dung. Cyanobacteria are described by NCERT under the eubacteria ('true bacteria').
steps: (c) false; hot springs = thermoacidophiles; halophiles = salty areas
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Monera (archaebacteria, eubacteria)
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a) and (b) only

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of both viruses and viroids, but NOT of prions?

options.text: They have a protein coat around the nucleic acid.
They consist of abnormally folded protein.
They contain both DNA and RNA.
They contain nucleic acid as their genetic material.

solution.explanation: Viruses contain genetic material that is either RNA or DNA, within a protein capsid. A viroid is a free RNA that lacks the protein coat found in viruses. Prions are infectious agents consisting of abnormally folded protein. So only viruses and viroids carry nucleic acid as genetic material.
steps: Virus: RNA or DNA + protein coat
Viroid: free RNA, no protein coat
solution.why_others_wrong: Viroids lack the protein coat. Abnormally folded protein describes prions. No virus contains both DNA and RNA, and a viroid has only RNA.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens
solution.final_answer: Option D: They contain nucleic acid as their genetic material.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Taking all the properties of life together, NCERT describes living organisms as:

options.text: isolated metabolic reactions that can be demonstrated in a test tube
systems that grow only by the accumulation of material on their surface
systems defined by reproduction, so that a non-reproducing organism is non-living
self-replicating, evolving and self-regulating interactive systems capable of responding to external stimuli

solution.explanation: NCERT concludes that living organisms are self-replicating, evolving and self-regulating interactive systems capable of responding to external stimuli. Isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are not living things, though they are surely living reactions. Growth by accumulation on the surface is how non-living objects grow. Reproduction is not an all-inclusive defining feature, since many organisms (mules, sterile worker bees, infertile couples) do not reproduce.
steps: Living organisms = self-replicating, evolving, self-regulating interactive systems
solution.why_others_wrong: In vitro reactions are not living things; surface accumulation is non-living growth; reproduction cannot be an all-inclusive defining characteristic.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Diversity in the Living World (what is living)
solution.final_answer: Option D: self-replicating, evolving and self-regulating interactive systems capable of responding to external stimuli

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the NCERT table of organisms with their taxonomic categories, how many taxonomic categories of mango lie between its genus Mangifera and its division Angiospermae (both excluded)?

solution.explanation: Mango: genus Mangifera, family Anacardiaceae, order Sapindales, class Dicotyledonae, division Angiospermae. Between the genus and the division (both excluded) lie the family, the order and the class.
steps: Hierarchy: genus - family - order - class - division
Between genus and division: family, order, class
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 leaves out one category (usually the class); 4 counts the genus or the division as well; 5 counts the whole list including both ends.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Taxonomic categories (table of organisms with their taxonomic categories)
solution.final_answer: Option A: 3

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following organisms are eukaryotic and can carry out photosynthesis?

(a) Chlamydomonas
(b) Nostoc
(c) Chlorella
(d) Euglena (in the presence of sunlight)
(e) Mucor

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Chlamydomonas and Chlorella are green algae (placed in Protista in the five kingdom system) and are photosynthetic eukaryotes. Euglena is a protist that is photosynthetic in the presence of sunlight. Nostoc is a cyanobacterium: photosynthetic but prokaryotic (Monera). Mucor is a fungus: eukaryotic but heterotrophic.
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option with (b) includes a prokaryote; an option with (e) includes a heterotrophic fungus.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Monera; Kingdom Protista; Kingdom Fungi
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Nostoc and Chlamydomonas, though both photosynthetic, are placed in different kingdoms in the five kingdom classification.
Reason (R): Cell structure (prokaryotic or eukaryotic) is one of the main criteria used by Whittaker to separate kingdoms.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Criteria of the five kingdom system
solution.explanation: Whittaker's main criteria were cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships. Nostoc is prokaryotic and goes to Monera; Chlamydomonas is a eukaryote and goes to Protista. The same mode of nutrition does not keep them together because they differ in cell structure.
steps: The prokaryotic/eukaryotic difference is why they are separated, so R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Introduction (five kingdom classification); Kingdom Monera; Kingdom Protista
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In ascomycetes, both the asexual spores (conidia) and the sexual spores (ascospores) are produced exogenously.
Statement II: In deuteromycetes, the mycelium is septate and branched.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Spore formation in ascomycetes; mycelium of deuteromycetes
solution.explanation: In ascomycetes the asexual spores, conidia, are produced exogenously on special mycelium called conidiophores, but the sexual spores, ascospores, are produced endogenously in sac-like asci. Deuteromycetes reproduce only by asexual spores (conidia), and their mycelium is septate and branched.
steps: Statement I: false; ascospores are endogenous
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi (Ascomycetes, Deuteromycetes)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In some fungi, an intervening dikaryotic stage (n + n) occurs between plasmogamy and karyogamy. In which of the following pairs can BOTH fungi show this stage?

solution.explanation: The dikaryotic stage occurs in ascomycetes and basidiomycetes. Claviceps is an ascomycete and Agaricus a basidiomycete, so both can show it. Mucor, Albugo and Rhizopus are phycomycetes; Alternaria and Trichoderma are deuteromycetes, whose sexual stages are not known.
solution.why_others_wrong: Mucor and Albugo are both phycomycetes; Alternaria and Trichoderma are deuteromycetes with no known sexual stage; in the last pair Rhizopus is a phycomycete.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi
solution.final_answer: Option B: Claviceps and Agaricus

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (group) with List-II (asexual reproduction as described in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Phycomycetes
B. Ascomycetes
C. Basidiomycetes
D. Bacteria

List-II:
I. Mainly by fission; spores may form under unfavourable conditions
II. Motile zoospores or non-motile aplanospores formed endogenously in a sporangium
III. Asexual spores generally not found; fragmentation common
IV. Conidia produced exogenously on conidiophores

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Asexual reproduction in fungi and bacteria
solution.explanation: Phycomycetes reproduce asexually by zoospores (motile) or aplanospores (non-motile), produced endogenously in a sporangium. Ascomycetes form conidia exogenously on conidiophores. In basidiomycetes asexual spores are generally not found, but vegetative reproduction by fragmentation is common. Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission; under unfavourable conditions they may produce spores.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes exchange the endogenous and exogenous spores of phycomycetes and ascomycetes, give basidiomycetes the bacterial mode, or give them conidia.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Monera; Kingdom Fungi
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The plant body of a brown alga is usually attached to the substratum by a holdfast and has a stalk, the stipe. Its leaf-like photosynthetic organ is called the:

solution.explanation: In Phaeophyceae the plant body is usually attached to the substratum by a holdfast, and has a stalk, the stipe, and a leaf-like photosynthetic organ, the frond.
solution.why_others_wrong: Thallus is the general term for an undifferentiated plant body. Rhizoids attach bryophytes, not brown algae. A sporophyll is a leaf-like appendage bearing sporangia in pteridophytes and gymnosperms.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (Phaeophyceae)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT divides algae into three main classes. Which of the following is NOT one of them?

solution.explanation: Algae are divided into three main classes: Chlorophyceae (green algae), Phaeophyceae (brown algae) and Rhodophyceae (red algae). Chrysophytes (diatoms and golden algae) are placed by NCERT in kingdom Protista, not among these classes.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other three options are exactly the three main classes of algae named in NCERT.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae
solution.final_answer: Option B: Chrysophyceae

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a pteridophyte, the zygote formed after fusion of the male gamete with the egg in the archegonium develops into:

options.text: a prothallus, which is the dominant phase
a multicellular, well-differentiated sporophyte, which is the dominant phase
a protonema, from which leafy shoots arise
a female gametophyte retained within the megasporangium

solution.concept: Fate of the zygote in pteridophytes
solution.explanation: The gametophytes bear antheridia and archegonia. Water carries the antherozoids to the mouth of the archegonium, and fusion of a male gamete with the egg forms the zygote. The zygote then produces a multicellular, well-differentiated sporophyte, which is the dominant phase of pteridophytes.
solution.why_others_wrong: The prothallus is the gametophyte, formed from a spore and not the dominant phase. The protonema belongs to mosses. A female gametophyte develops from a megaspore, not from the zygote.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Pteridophytes
solution.final_answer: Option B: a multicellular, well-differentiated sporophyte, which is the dominant phase

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

Unlike bryophytes and pteridophytes, the male and female gametophytes of gymnosperms do not have an independent free-living existence; they remain within the sporangia retained on the sporophytes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (term) with List-II (meaning in pteridophytes).

List-I:
A. Sporophyll
B. Strobilus
C. Prothallus
D. Microphyll

List-II:
I. Small leaf, as in Selaginella
II. Leaf-like appendage that subtends sporangia
III. Compact structure formed by sporophylls
IV. Small, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The pteridophyte sporophyte bears sporangia subtended by leaf-like appendages called sporophylls. In some (Selaginella, Equisetum) the sporophylls form distinct compact structures called strobili or cones. The spores germinate into small, multicellular, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophytes called prothalli. Small leaves, as in Selaginella, are microphylls; large ones, as in ferns, are macrophylls.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes exchange sporophyll and strobilus, prothallus and microphyll, or strobilus and prothallus.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Pteridophytes
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a green alga (Chlorophyceae)?

solution.explanation: NCERT's examples of Chlorophyceae are Chlamydomonas, Volvox, Ulothrix, Spirogyra and Chara. Dictyota is a brown alga, while Polysiphonia and Gracilaria are red algae.
steps: Green algae: Chlamydomonas, Volvox, Ulothrix, Spirogyra, Chara

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are true of BOTH brown algae (Phaeophyceae) and red algae (Rhodophyceae)?

(a) The majority of members are marine.
(b) Some members produce hydrocolloids (water-holding substances) that are used commercially.
(c) Their motile cells bear two unequal, lateral flagella.
(d) Chlorophyll a is present.
(e) Food is stored as floridean starch.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Brown algae are found primarily in marine habitats, and the majority of red algae are marine. Certain marine brown and red algae produce large amounts of hydrocolloids: algin (brown algae) and carrageen (red algae), used commercially. Chlorophyll a is present in both. Two unequal lateral flagella occur only in brown algae; red algae have no flagella. Floridean starch is the food of red algae only; brown algae store mannitol or laminarin.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (Phaeophyceae, Rhodophyceae; table of divisions of algae)

questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In Chlorophyceae, sexual reproduction may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous.
Statement II: In Rhodophyceae, sexual reproduction may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In green algae, sexual reproduction shows considerable variation in the type and formation of sex cells, and it may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous. In red algae, sexual reproduction (by non-motile gametes) is oogamous and is accompanied by complex post-fertilisation developments.
steps: Statement II: false; red algae are oogamous
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (Chlorophyceae, Rhodophyceae)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, which of the following is a feature of mosses that is NOT described for liverworts?

options.text: Asexual reproduction by gemmae formed in gemma cups
A sporophyte differentiated into foot, seta and capsule
A protonema stage of the gametophyte that develops directly from a spore

solution.explanation: The moss gametophyte has two stages: the protonema, a creeping, green, branched, frequently filamentous stage that develops directly from a spore, and the leafy stage, which develops from the secondary protonema as a lateral bud. Liverworts have a thalloid or leafy gametophyte with no protonema stage described. Gemmae in gemma cups are a liverwort feature; a sporophyte with foot, seta and capsule and multicellular sex organs are found in both.

solution.why_others_wrong: Gemmae in gemma cups are described for liverworts. The liverwort sporophyte is also differentiated into foot, seta and capsule. All bryophytes have multicellular sex organs.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes (liverworts, mosses)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A protonema stage of the gametophyte that develops directly from a spore

Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In liverworts, the male and female sex organs are produced either on the same thallus or on different thalli.
Reason (R): The sporophyte of a liverwort is free-living and independent of the gametophyte.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Sex organs and sporophyte of liverworts
solution.explanation: During sexual reproduction in liverworts, male and female sex organs are produced either on the same or on different thalli. The sporophyte, differentiated into foot, seta and capsule, is not free-living: in bryophytes it remains attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte and derives nourishment from it.
steps: R: false; the bryophyte sporophyte depends on the gametophyte
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes (liverworts)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a gymnosperm, each ovule has one megaspore mother cell. If the megaspore mother cells of 6 ovules complete their division, how many megaspores are formed in all, and how many of these develop into female gametophytes?

solution.explanation: The megaspore mother cell is differentiated from one of the cells of the nucellus and divides meiotically to form four megaspores. One of the megaspores enclosed within the megasporangium develops into a multicellular female gametophyte bearing two or more archegonia.
solution.why_others_wrong: 24 gametophytes assumes every megaspore develops; 12 treats the division as giving two cells; 6 megaspores ignores that meiosis gives four.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option A: 24 megaspores; 6 female gametophytes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs of pteridophytes belong to the same class?

solution.explanation: NCERT divides pteridophytes into four classes: Psilopsida (Psilotum), Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum) and Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum). Selaginella and Lycopodium are both Lycopsida.
solution.why_others_wrong: Psilotum (Psilopsida) and Equisetum (Sphenopsida) differ; Equisetum and Adiantum (Pteropsida) differ; Selaginella (Lycopsida) and Dryopteris (Pteropsida) differ.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Pteridophytes
solution.final_answer: Option B: Selaginella and Lycopodium

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:

Statement I: Members of both Chlorophyceae and Phaeophyceae have motile cells, but their flagella differ: 2-8, equal and apical in the former, and 2, unequal and lateral in the latter.
Statement II: Like the red algae, members of Phaeophyceae store their food as floridean starch.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Flagella and stored food in algae
solution.explanation: NCERT's table of the divisions of algae gives Chlorophyceae 2-8 equal, apical flagella and Phaeophyceae 2 unequal, lateral flagella; Rhodophyceae have none. Stored food is starch in Chlorophyceae, mannitol or laminarin in Phaeophyceae and floridean starch in Rhodophyceae.
steps: Statement II: false; brown algae store mannitol or laminarin
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (table of divisions of algae and their main characteristics)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (feature) with List-II (plant group).

A. Naked seeds
B. First terrestrial plants with xylem and phloem

List-II:
I. Algae
II. Bryophytes
III. Pteridophytes
IV. Gymnosperms

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Gymnosperms have ovules not enclosed by an ovary wall, so the seeds are naked. Pteridophytes are, evolutionarily, the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues, xylem and phloem. In bryophytes the sporophyte is not free-living; it is attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte and derives nourishment from it. In algae the most common asexual spores are the flagellated zoospores.

Reason (R): In gymnosperms, the megaspore mother cell divides meiotically to form four megaspores.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Gymnosperms are heterosporous. The megaspore mother cell, differentiated from a nucellus cell, divides meiotically to form four megaspores. One megaspore, enclosed within the megasporangium, develops into the multicellular female gametophyte, which is retained within the megasporangium; it is not shed and is not free-living.
steps: A: false; the female gametophyte develops within the megasporangium
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which sequence correctly shows the development of a moss from a spore up to the formation of sex organs?

options.text: Spore -> leafy stage -> protonema -> antheridia and archegonia on the protonema
Spore -> prothallus -> leafy stage -> antheridia and archegonia on the prothallus
Spore -> protonema -> capsule -> leafy stage -> antheridia and archegonia on the capsule
Spore -> protonema -> lateral bud on the secondary protonema -> leafy stage -> antheridia and archegonia at the apex of the leafy shoots

solution.explanation: The protonema develops directly from a spore; it is a creeping, green, branched, frequently filamentous stage. The leafy stage develops from the secondary protonema as a lateral bud and bears spirally arranged leaves. The sex organs, antheridia and archegonia, are produced at the apex of the leafy shoots.
steps: Secondary protonema -> lateral bud -> leafy stage
Sex organs at the shoot apex
solution.why_others_wrong: The leafy stage comes after, not before, the protonema. A prothallus is a pteridophyte gametophyte. The capsule is part of the sporophyte, formed after fertilisation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes (mosses)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Spore -> protonema -> lateral bud on the secondary protonema -> leafy stage -> antheridia and archegonia at the apex of the leafy shoots

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following alga - stored food pairs is INCORRECT?

solution.concept: Stored food of the classes of algae
solution.explanation: Stored food: Chlorophyceae, starch; Phaeophyceae, mannitol or laminarin; Rhodophyceae, floridean starch. Porphyra is a red alga, Laminaria and Fucus are brown algae, and Chara is a green alga. Fucus, being brown, stores mannitol or laminarin, not floridean starch.
solution.why_others_wrong: Porphyra (red) does store floridean starch; Laminaria (brown) stores mannitol or laminarin; Chara (green) stores starch.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (table of divisions of algae and their main characteristics)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Fucus - floridean starch

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Of the four whorls of a typical flower, which are described by NCERT as the reproductive organs?

solution.explanation: A typical flower has four whorls: calyx, corolla, androecium and gynoecium. Calyx and corolla are accessory organs, while androecium and gynoecium are reproductive organs.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, the main function of the stem is:

options.text: absorption of water and minerals from the soil
spreading out branches bearing leaves, flowers and fruits
protecting the flower in the bud stage
anchoring the plant parts firmly in the soil

solution.explanation: The main function of the stem is spreading out branches bearing leaves, flowers and fruits. It conducts water, minerals and photosynthates. Some stems also store food, give support and protection, and help in vegetative propagation.
steps: Main function: bearing and spreading out branches with leaves, flowers and fruits
Also: conduction of water, minerals and photosynthates

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The arrangement of flowers on the floral axis is termed:

solution.explanation: A flower is a modified shoot. The arrangement of flowers on the floral axis is termed inflorescence; depending on whether the apex grows into a flower or continues to grow, it is cymose or racemose.
steps: Arrangement of flowers on the floral axis = inflorescence
solution.why_others_wrong: Aestivation is the arrangement of sepals or petals in a bud; placentation is the arrangement of ovules in the ovary; phyllotaxy is the arrangement of leaves on the stem or branch.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:

B. Thalamus

II. Calyx and corolla when they are not distinct
III. Stalk of the flower
IV. Swollen end of the stalk on which the floral whorls are borne

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The four whorls of a typical flower are arranged successively on the swollen end of the stalk or pedicel, called the thalamus or receptacle. Flowers with a bract, a reduced leaf found at the base of the pedicel, are bracteate. When calyx and corolla are not distinct, as in lily, they are termed the perianth.

Bract -> reduced leaf at the pedicel base

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Each carpel of the gynoecium is made up of:

solution.explanation: The gynoecium is the female reproductive part of the flower and is made up of one or more carpels. A carpel consists of three parts, namely stigma, style and ovary. The ovary bears one or more ovules attached to a flattened, cushion-like placenta.
solution.why_others_wrong: Filament and anther make a stamen. The placenta lies inside the ovary and is not a separate part replacing it. The pedicel is the stalk of the flower.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Parts of a Flower (gynoecium)

endospermous, with a bulky endosperm separated from the embryo by an aleurone layer

Corolla outermost; androecium in the centre
Androecium outermost; gynoecium in the centre
Calyx outermost; gynoecium in the centre

Calyx, corolla, androecium and gynoecium are drawn in successive whorls, calyx being the outermost and gynoecium being in the centre.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
The floral formula of a family is % ⚥ K(5) C1+2+(2) A(9)+1 G1. Which of the following conclusions drawn from it are correct?

(b) The calyx is gamosepalous.

(d) The gynoecium is syncarpous.

(e) false: (9) + 1 means nine united, one free

questions.question_text:

Statement II: In both Fabaceae and Solanaceae, the seeds are endospermous.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

Which of the following statements about the cymose type of inflorescence are correct?

(a) The main axis terminates in a flower.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the phloem of angiosperms, companion cells are:

options.text: dead sclerenchymatous cells with very thick, lignified walls
specialised parenchymatous cells closely associated with the sieve tube elements
the sieve cells found in the phloem of gymnosperms
thin-walled xylem cells that store tannins

solution.explanation: Companion cells are specialised parenchymatous cells closely associated with the sieve tube elements. The sieve tube elements and companion cells are connected by pit fields in their common longitudinal walls, and the nucleus of the companion cell controls the functions of the sieve tube, which lacks a nucleus at maturity.
steps: Companion cell = specialised parenchyma cell beside a sieve tube element
solution.why_others_wrong: Dead, thick-walled lignified cells describe sclerenchyma (such as phloem fibres). Gymnosperms have sieve cells and albuminous cells and lack companion cells. Tannin-storing thin-walled xylem cells are xylem parenchyma.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (phloem)
solution.final_answer: Option B: specialised parenchymatous cells closely associated with the sieve tube elements

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a dorsiventral (dicotyledonous) leaf, the vascular bundles are surrounded by a layer of:

solution.concept: Vascular bundles of a dorsiventral leaf
solution.explanation: The vascular system of a dorsiventral leaf includes the vascular bundles seen in the veins and the midrib. The vascular bundles are surrounded by a layer of thick-walled bundle sheath cells.
steps: Dorsiventral leaf: bundles in veins and midrib
Each surrounded by thick-walled bundle sheath cells
solution.why_others_wrong: Bulliform cells are large epidermal cells of grass leaves. Casparian strips belong to the endodermis of the root. Semi-lunar sclerenchyma patches are the pericycle of the dicot stem.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants (dorsiventral leaf)
solution.final_answer: Option D: thick-walled bundle sheath cells

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Root hairs and trichomes both belong to the epidermal tissue system.
Statement II: Root hairs are usually multicellular, whereas the trichomes of the shoot system are unicellular.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The epidermal tissue system is made of epidermal cells, stomata and the epidermal appendages, the trichomes and hairs. Root hairs are unicellular elongations of the epidermal cells that absorb water and minerals. The trichomes of the shoot system are usually multicellular; they may be branched or unbranched, soft or stiff, and even secretory.
steps: Statement II: false; root hairs are unicellular, trichomes usually multicellular
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissue System (epidermal tissue system)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A simple permanent tissue has oval, spherical or polygonal cells whose walls are thickened at the corners by deposition of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin. The cells often contain chloroplasts, and intercellular spaces are absent. The tissue is:

solution.explanation: Collenchyma cells are thickened at the corners due to a deposition of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin. They may be oval, spherical or polygonal, often contain chloroplasts and assimilate food when chloroplasts are present. Intercellular spaces are absent. Collenchyma gives mechanical support to growing parts such as the young stem and the petiole.
steps: Corner thickening of cellulose, hemicellulose, pectin = collenchyma
solution.why_others_wrong: Parenchyma has thin cellulose walls; sclerenchyma has thick lignified walls; xylem parenchyma is a thin-walled storage tissue of the xylem, a complex tissue.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (simple tissues: collenchyma)
solution.final_answer: Option A: collenchyma

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (meristem or bud) with List-II (role described in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Apical meristem
B. Intercalary meristem
C. Lateral meristem
D. Axillary bud

List-II:
I. Can form a branch or a flower
II. Produces the secondary tissues
III. Produces the primary tissues at the tips of roots and shoots
IV. Regenerates parts removed by grazing herbivores in grasses

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Apical meristems occur at the tips of roots and shoots and produce primary tissues. Intercalary meristems occur in grasses and regenerate parts removed by grazing herbivores. Lateral meristems, in the mature regions of roots and shoots, are responsible for producing the secondary tissues. Axillary buds, formed from cells left behind by the shoot apical meristem, are capable of forming a branch or a flower.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap apical and intercalary, lateral and axillary bud, or intercalary and lateral.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (meristematic tissues)
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Sclereids are commonly found in the seed coats of legumes.
Reason (R): Sclereids are living cells with thin cellulose walls.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Sclereids are spherical, oval or cylindrical, highly thickened dead cells with very narrow cavities (lumen). They are commonly found in the fruit walls of nuts, the pulp of fruits like guava, pear and sapota, the seed coats of legumes and the leaves of tea.
steps: R: false; sclereids are dead and highly thickened
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (simple tissues: sclerenchyma)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
The section of a leaf shows a mesophyll differentiated into palisade parenchyma on the adaxial side and spongy parenchyma below it, with more stomata on the lower epidermis than on the upper. Which of the following conclusions are correct?

(a) It is a dorsiventral (dicotyledonous) leaf.
(b) Its vascular bundles vary in size, depending on the size of the veins.
(c) Large, empty, colourless bulliform cells are present along its veins in the adaxial epidermis.
(d) Each stoma is bounded by two bean-shaped guard cells.
(e) Its spongy parenchyma cells are loosely arranged, with large spaces and air cavities.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A mesophyll with adaxial palisade and abaxial spongy parenchyma, and more stomata on the abaxial epidermis, marks a dorsiventral (dicot) leaf. The size of its vascular bundles depends on the size of the veins, which vary in thickness in the reticulate venation of dicot leaves. Dicot guard cells are bean-shaped. The spongy parenchyma cells are oval or round, loosely arranged, with large spaces and air cavities. Bulliform cells are a feature of grass (isobilateral) leaves.
steps: (c) false; bulliform cells occur in grasses
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants (leaves); The Tissue System
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b), (d) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (tissue) with List-II (function described in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Xylem
B. Phloem
C. Collenchyma
D. Sclerenchyma

List-II:
I. Mechanical support to organs
II. Transport of food materials, usually from the leaves to other parts
III. Mechanical support to growing parts such as the young stem and the petiole
IV. Conduction of water and minerals from the roots to the stem and leaves

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Xylem conducts water and minerals from the roots to the stem and leaves (and gives mechanical strength). Phloem transports food materials, usually from the leaves to other parts of the plant. Collenchyma gives mechanical support to the growing parts, such as the young stem and the petiole of a leaf. Sclerenchyma provides mechanical support to organs.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap xylem and phloem, collenchyma and sclerenchyma, or xylem and collenchyma.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Both tracheids and vessel members are devoid of protoplasm at maturity.
Statement II: Xylem fibres have thin walls and a wide central lumen.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Tracheids are elongated, tube-like cells with thick, lignified walls and tapering ends; they are dead and without protoplasm. Vessel members, with lignified walls and a large central cavity, are also devoid of protoplasm. Xylem fibres have highly thickened walls and obliterated central lumens.
steps: Statement II: false; xylem fibres have very thick walls and obliterated lumens
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (complex tissues: xylem)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A transverse section of a young root shows radial vascular bundles with two to four xylem and phloem patches, a small pith and an endodermis with Casparian strips. In this organ, lateral roots are initiated in the:

solution.concept: Dicot root: origin of lateral roots
solution.explanation: Two to four xylem and phloem patches and a small or inconspicuous pith identify a dicot root. Next to the endodermis, towards the inside, lie a few layers of thick-walled parenchymatous cells, the pericycle. Initiation of lateral roots takes place in these cells.
steps: Lateral roots arise in the pericycle
solution.why_others_wrong: The endodermis is the innermost cortical layer with Casparian strips; the epiblema is the outermost layer bearing root hairs; conjunctive tissue is the parenchyma between xylem and phloem.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants (dicotyledonous root)
solution.final_answer: Option B: pericycle

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Axillary buds are capable of forming a branch or a flower.
Reason (R): Axillary buds arise from the activity of the lateral meristem.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: During the formation of leaves and elongation of the stem, some cells 'left behind' from the shoot apical meristem constitute the axillary bud. Such buds are present in the axils of leaves and are capable of forming a branch or a flower. The lateral meristem is a cylindrical meristem in the mature regions of roots and shoots.
steps: R: false; axillary buds come from cells left behind by the shoot apical meristem
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (meristematic tissues)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a dicot root, the conjunctive tissue is a part of the stele.
Reason (R): All tissues on the inner side of the endodermis constitute the stele, and the conjunctive tissue lies between the xylem and the phloem, inside the endodermis.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In the dicot root, all tissues on the inner side of the endodermis, such as the pericycle, vascular bundles and pith, constitute the stele. The conjunctive tissue is the parenchyma lying between the xylem and the phloem, which are within the endodermis; so it falls within the stele.
steps: Being inside the endodermis is exactly what makes a tissue part of the stele
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants (dicotyledonous root)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (feature seen in a section) with List-II (organ).

List-I:
A. Water-containing cavities within the vascular bundles
B. Semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma above the phloem
C. Large, well-developed pith with usually more than six xylem bundles
D. Stomata on both surfaces and an undifferentiated mesophyll

List-II:
I. Isobilateral leaf
II. Monocot root
III. Dicot stem
IV. Monocot stem

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Water-containing cavities in the bundles are a feature of the monocot stem. Semi-lunar sclerenchyma patches above the phloem form the pericycle of the dicot stem. A monocot root has a large, well-developed pith and usually more than six (polyarch) xylem bundles. An isobilateral leaf has stomata on both surfaces and a mesophyll not differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap the two stems, the monocot root and the isobilateral leaf, or the dicot stem and the monocot root.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Phloem fibres (bast fibres) are generally absent in the primary phloem but are found in the secondary phloem.
Statement II: Phloem fibres are much elongated and unbranched, with pointed, needle-like apices and quite thick walls.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Phloem fibres (bast fibres) are made up of sclerenchymatous cells. They are generally absent in the primary phloem but are found in the secondary phloem. They are much elongated, unbranched and have pointed, needle-like apices, and their cell wall is quite thick. At maturity they lose their protoplasm and become dead.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (complex tissues: phloem)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In which of the following pairs do BOTH cells lack a nucleus at maturity?

options.text: Companion cell and sieve tube element
Xylem parenchyma cell and vessel member

solution.concept: Cells without a nucleus at maturity
solution.explanation: Tracheids are dead and without protoplasm, so they have no nucleus. A mature sieve tube element is living but possesses only peripheral cytoplasm and a large vacuole and lacks a nucleus; its functions are controlled by the nucleus of the companion cell. Companion cells, collenchyma cells and xylem parenchyma cells are living cells with nuclei.
steps: Sieve tube element: living but no nucleus
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong pair includes a living, nucleated cell: the companion cell, the collenchyma cell or the xylem parenchyma cell.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (xylem and phloem)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Tracheid and sieve tube element

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following lie on the inner side of the endodermis in a dicot stem?

(a) Pericycle
(b) Medullary rays
(c) Hypodermis
(d) Vascular bundles
(e) Pith

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Arrangement of tissues in the dicot stem
solution.explanation: In the dicot stem, the cortex has three sub-zones: the outer collenchymatous hypodermis, the cortical layers and the innermost endodermis. Inside the endodermis lie the pericycle (semi-lunar sclerenchyma patches above the phloem), the ring of vascular bundles, the medullary rays between the bundles and the central pith.
steps: Outside the endodermis: epidermis, hypodermis, cortical layers
Inside: pericycle, vascular bundles, medullary rays, pith
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants (dicotyledonous stem)
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b), (d) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a chloroplast, the flat membranous tubules that connect the thylakoids of different grana are called:

solution.explanation: The space limited by the inner membrane of the chloroplast is the stroma. A number of organised, flattened membranous sacs, the thylakoids, are present in the stroma and are arranged in stacks like piles of coins called grana. Flat membranous tubules called stroma lamellae connect the thylakoids of the different grana.
steps: Stroma lamellae connect thylakoids of different grana
solution.why_others_wrong: Cristae are infoldings of the inner mitochondrial membrane. Mesosomes and chromatophores are membrane extensions of prokaryotic cells.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (plastids)
solution.final_answer: Option D: stroma lamellae

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer of the cell membrane. This ability to move within the membrane is measured as its:

solution.explanation: In the fluid mosaic model of Singer and Nicolson (1972), the quasi-fluid nature of the lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer. This ability to move within the membrane is measured as its fluidity. The fluid nature is important for functions like cell growth, formation of intercellular junctions, secretion, endocytosis and cell division.
steps: Lateral movement within the membrane is measured as fluidity
solution.why_others_wrong: Selective permeability refers to which molecules can cross the membrane. Osmosis is diffusion of water. Active transport is energy-dependent movement against a concentration gradient.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (cell membrane)
solution.final_answer: Option B: fluidity

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Every chromosome has a primary constriction, the centromere. The disc-shaped structures present on the sides of the centromere are called:

solution.explanation: Every chromosome essentially has a primary constriction, the centromere, on the sides of which disc-shaped structures called kinetochores are present.
steps: Disc-shaped structures on its sides = kinetochores
solution.why_others_wrong: A satellite is a small chromosome fragment set off by a non-staining secondary constriction. Centrioles lie in the centrosome of animal cells, and nucleoli are bodies in the nucleoplasm.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (nucleus)
solution.final_answer: Option B: kinetochores

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Normally there is only one nucleus per cell, although variations in the number of nuclei are also frequently observed.
Statement II: The nucleus contains one or more spherical structures called nucleoli in the nucleoplasm.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT states that normally there is only one nucleus per cell, though variations in the number of nuclei are also frequently observed. The nuclear matrix or nucleoplasm contains the nucleolus and chromatin; the nucleoli are spherical structures present in the nucleoplasm.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (nucleus)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (plastid) with List-II (content).

List-I:
A. Amyloplasts
B. Elaioplasts
C. Aleuroplasts
D. Chromoplasts

List-II:
I. Fat-soluble carotenoid pigments
II. Proteins
III. Starch (carbohydrates)
IV. Oils and fats

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids of varied shapes and sizes with stored nutrients: amyloplasts store carbohydrates (starch), elaioplasts store oils and fats, and aleuroplasts store proteins. Chromoplasts contain fat-soluble carotenoid pigments such as carotene and xanthophylls.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap amyloplasts and elaioplasts, aleuroplasts and chromoplasts, or elaioplasts and aleuroplasts.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (plastids)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In animal cells, lipid-like steroidal hormones are synthesised in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum.
Reason (R): The smooth endoplasmic reticulum is the major site for the synthesis of lipids.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The endoplasmic reticulum that does not bear ribosomes appears smooth (SER). The SER is the major site for the synthesis of lipid; accordingly, in animal cells, lipid-like steroidal hormones are synthesised in the SER.
steps: Steroidal hormones are lipid-like, so they are made where lipids are made
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (endoplasmic reticulum)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
In which of the following locations would you expect 70S ribosomes?

(a) The cytoplasm of a bacterium
(b) The stroma of a chloroplast
(c) The matrix of a mitochondrion
(d) The cytoplasm of an onion root cell
(e) The rough endoplasmic reticulum of a liver cell

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Prokaryotic ribosomes are of the 70S type. The chloroplast stroma contains ribosomes smaller (70S) than the cytoplasmic ones (80S), and the mitochondrial matrix contains 70S ribosomes. The cytoplasm of an eukaryotic cell, including ribosomes on the RER, has 80S ribosomes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Prokaryotic Cells (ribosomes); Eukaryotic Cells (mitochondria, plastids, ribosomes)
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Transport of a few ions or molecules across the membrane from lower to higher concentration is an energy-dependent process that uses ATP, as in the Na+/K+ pump.
Statement II: Neutral solutes move across the membrane by simple diffusion against their concentration gradient.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Neutral solutes may move across the membrane by simple diffusion along the concentration gradient, from higher to lower concentration. A few ions or molecules are transported against their concentration gradient, from lower to higher concentration; this is an energy-dependent process using ATP, called active transport, e.g. the Na+/K+ pump.
steps: Statement II: false; simple diffusion is along the gradient
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (cell membrane)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (cell activity) with List-II (structure chiefly concerned).

List-I:
A. A gland cell synthesising and secreting much protein
B. Formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids
C. Osmoregulation and excretion in Amoeba
D. Accumulating ions in the vacuole above their cytoplasmic concentration

List-II:
I. Contractile vacuole
II. Tonoplast
III. Rough endoplasmic reticulum
IV. Golgi apparatus

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The RER is frequently observed in cells actively involved in protein synthesis and secretion. The Golgi apparatus is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids. In Amoeba the contractile vacuole is important for osmoregulation and excretion. The tonoplast facilitates the transport of a number of ions and other materials against concentration gradients into the vacuole, so their concentration is significantly higher in the vacuole than in the cytoplasm.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap RER and Golgi, the contractile vacuole and tonoplast, or Golgi and the contractile vacuole.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (endomembrane system)
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, a single human cell has an approximately two-metre-long thread of DNA distributed among its forty-six chromosomes. On average, about how long is the DNA of one chromosome?

solution.concept: Length of DNA in human chromosomes
solution.explanation: The DNA of a human cell, about 2 m long, is distributed among 46 chromosomes (23 pairs). The average length per chromosome is 2 m / 46 = 200 cm / 46, about 4.3 cm.
solution.why_others_wrong: 8.7 cm divides by the 23 pairs instead of the 46 chromosomes; 43 cm and 0.43 cm are errors of a factor of 10 in converting metres to centimetres.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (nucleus)
solution.final_answer: Option D: About 4.3 cm

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Mesosomes increase the surface area of the plasma membrane and its enzymatic content.
Reason (R): Mesosomes are double-membrane-bound organelles, like mitochondria.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Mesosomes are a special membranous structure formed by extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell, in the form of vesicles, tubules and lamellae. They help in cell wall formation, DNA replication and its distribution to daughter cells, respiration and secretion, and increase the surface area of the plasma membrane and its enzymatic content. Prokaryotes have no membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria.
steps: R: false; mesosomes are extensions of the plasma membrane, not organelles
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Prokaryotic Cells (cell envelope and its modifications)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (structure) with List-II (organisation).

List-I:
A. Axoneme of a cilium
B. Centriole
C. Bacterial flagellum
D. Basal body

List-II:
I. Filament, hook and basal body
II. Centriole-like structure from which a cilium or flagellum emerges
III. Nine peripheral doublets around a central pair of microtubules
IV. Nine evenly spaced peripheral triplet fibrils of tubulin, like a cartwheel

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The axoneme of a cilium or flagellum has nine pairs of doublets of radially arranged peripheral microtubules and a pair of centrally located microtubules (9 + 2). A centriole has an organisation like a cartwheel, made of nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils of tubulin, each a triplet. A bacterial flagellum has a filament, a hook and a basal body. Cilia and flagella emerge from centriole-like structures called basal bodies.
steps: Bacterial flagellum -> filament, hook, basal body
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap the axoneme and centriole, the bacterial flagellum and basal body, or the axoneme and bacterial flagellum.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (cilia and flagella; centrosome); Prokaryotic Cells
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
A cell has a nucleus with a nuclear envelope and a centrosome with two centrioles, but no cell wall and no plastids. Which of the following conclusions about it are correct?

(a) It is a eukaryotic cell.
(b) Its outer boundary is the plasma membrane.
(c) It has a large central vacuole.
(d) Its centrioles can give rise to the spindle fibres during cell division.
(e) All its ribosomes are of the 70S type.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A nucleus bounded by a nuclear envelope marks a eukaryotic cell; centrioles with no cell wall or plastids mark an animal cell. Its delimiting outer structure is the cell membrane. Plant cells, not animal cells, have a large central vacuole. In animal cells the centrioles give rise to the spindle fibres of the spindle apparatus. The cytoplasmic ribosomes of eukaryotes are 80S.
steps: (c) false: large central vacuole is a plant-cell feature
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells

questions.subject: Botany

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Two neighbouring mature plant cells each have a primary and a secondary wall. Which sequence correctly shows the layers met in going from the plasma membrane of one cell to the plasma membrane of the other?

Middle lamella -> primary wall -> secondary wall -> primary wall -> middle lamella
Secondary wall -> middle lamella -> primary wall -> middle lamella -> secondary wall
Secondary wall -> primary wall -> middle lamella -> primary wall -> secondary wall

solution.concept: Layers of the plant cell wall
solution.explanation: The cell wall of a young plant cell, the primary wall, is capable of growth. Secondary wall is formed on the inner (towards the membrane) side of the cell. The middle lamella, mainly calcium pectate, holds or glues the different neighbouring cells together. So from one plasma membrane outward: secondary wall, primary wall, then the shared middle lamella, then the other cell's primary and secondary walls.

Middle lamella lies between the walls of neighbouring cells

the axoneme of a cilium only

Centriole: hub -> radial spokes -> peripheral triplets

questions.subject: Botany

solution.explanation: Mitosis (karyokinesis) is divided into four stages: prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase. Cytokinesis, the division of the cytoplasm, follows.

Which of the following take place during prophase of mitosis?

(e) Each centrosome radiates out microtubules called asters.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Prophase is marked by the initiation of condensation of the chromosomal material. The centrosome, which had duplicated during interphase, now begins to move towards opposite poles, and each centrosome radiates out microtubules called asters. Alignment on the metaphase plate happens in metaphase, and splitting of centromeres in anaphase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a dividing cell, the nuclear envelope has completely disintegrated, the condensation of chromosomes is complete, the chromosomes are spread through the cytoplasm, and spindle fibres are attaching to their kinetochores as they move to the spindle equator. The cell is in:

solution.explanation: The complete disintegration of the nuclear envelope marks the start of metaphase. By this stage, condensation of chromosomes is complete and their morphology can be studied. Spindle fibres attach to the kinetochores of the chromosomes, which are moved to the spindle equator and aligned on the metaphase plate.
steps: Nuclear envelope fully gone + condensation complete + kinetochore attachment = metaphase
solution.why_others_wrong: In prophase the chromosomes are only beginning to condense and the envelope is still breaking down. In anaphase the centromeres split and chromatids move apart. Pachytene is a stage of prophase I, before the nuclear envelope breaks down.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (metaphase)

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

Pachytene is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules, the sites at which crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes. Zygotene is the stage of synapsis and formation of the synaptonemal complex.
steps: R: false; recombination nodules appear in pachytene

Statement II: In meiosis, recombination takes place between the sister chromatids of the same chromosome.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are described in NCERT as brought about by mitosis?

(a) Growth of multicellular organisms
(b) Restoration of the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio disturbed by cell growth
(c) Replacement of cells of the upper layer of the epidermis, the gut lining and blood cells
(d) Formation of gametes in animals
(e) Continuous growth of plants through divisions in the apical and lateral cambium

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Growth of multicellular organisms is due to mitosis. Cell growth disturbs the ratio between the nucleus and the cytoplasm, so the cell divides to restore the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio. Mitosis brings about cell repair: cells of the upper layer of the epidermis, the gut lining and blood cells are constantly replaced. Mitotic divisions in the apical and lateral cambium give continuous growth of plants throughout their life. Gametes in animals are formed through meiosis (gametogenesis).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Significance of Mitosis; Meiosis

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is seen at metaphase of mitosis and also at metaphase II of meiosis?

options.text: Bivalents align on the equatorial plate.
Microtubules from opposite poles attach to the two members of a pair of homologous chromosomes.
Chiasmata hold the homologous chromosomes together.
Microtubules from opposite poles attach to the kinetochores of the two sister chromatids of each chromosome.

solution.concept: Metaphase of mitosis compared with metaphase II
solution.explanation: At metaphase of mitosis, spindle fibres from one pole attach to the kinetochore of one chromatid and fibres from the opposite pole to its sister chromatid. At metaphase II the chromosomes align at the equator and microtubules from opposite poles attach to the kinetochores of sister chromatids. In metaphase I, by contrast, bivalents align and microtubules from opposite poles attach to the pair of homologous chromosomes.
steps: Mitosis metaphase and metaphase II: sister chromatids attached to opposite poles
solution.why_others_wrong: Alignment of bivalents and attachment to homologous pairs belong to metaphase I; chiasmata belong to prophase I and metaphase I, not to mitosis or meiosis II.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (metaphase); Meiosis (metaphase I, metaphase II)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Meiosis is important for the process of evolution.
Reason (R): Meiosis increases the genetic variability in the population of organisms from one generation to the next, and such variations are very important for evolution.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Meiosis conserves the specific chromosome number of each species across generations in sexually reproducing organisms. It also increases the genetic variability in the population from one generation to the next. Variations are very important for the process of evolution; this is why meiosis matters for evolution.
steps: Variability produced by meiosis is the reason it matters for evolution
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Significance of Meiosis
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Consider these events of meiosis: (i) separation of homologous chromosomes; (ii) terminalisation of chiasmata; (iii) splitting of the centromeres; (iv) formation of a dyad of cells; (v) alignment of bivalents on the equatorial plate. Which is the correct order?

solution.explanation: Terminalisation of chiasmata marks diakinesis, the end of prophase I. In metaphase I the bivalents align on the equatorial plate. In anaphase I the homologous chromosomes separate. Telophase I with cytokinesis gives a dyad of cells. In anaphase II the centromere of each chromosome splits.
solution.why_others_wrong: The first wrong order puts metaphase I before diakinesis; the second splits centromeres in meiosis I; the third separates homologues before they align and splits centromeres before the dyad forms.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis
solution.final_answer: Option D: (ii) -> (v) -> (i) -> (iv) -> (iii)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A cell in G2 phase and a cell at metaphase of mitosis of the same diploid plant have the same number of chromosomes and the same DNA content.
Statement II: Each nucleus at telophase I and a cell in G1 phase of the same plant have the same DNA content, though the telophase I nucleus has half as many chromosomes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: DNA content and chromosome number through division
solution.explanation: If the G1 cell has 2n chromosomes and 2C DNA, the S phase doubles the DNA to 4C without changing the chromosome number. So a G2 cell and a mitotic metaphase cell both have 2n chromosomes and 4C DNA. In meiosis I, homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together, so each telophase I nucleus has n chromosomes of two chromatids each: 2C DNA, the same as a G1 cell.
steps: Telophase I nucleus: n chromosomes x 2 chromatids = 2C = G1 DNA content
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle (phases); Meiosis
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (event in meiosis) with List-II (stage in which it occurs).

List-I:
A. Nucleolus disappears and nuclear envelope breaks down
B. Chiasmata first become visible
C. Sister chromatids separate
D. Homologous chromosomes separate

List-II:
I. Anaphase I
II. Diplotene
III. Anaphase II
IV. Diakinesis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: By the end of diakinesis the nucleolus disappears and the nuclear envelope breaks down. In diplotene the bivalents tend to separate except at the sites of crossovers; these X-shaped structures are the chiasmata. In anaphase I homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres. In anaphase II the centromeres split and sister chromatids separate.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap diakinesis and diplotene, the two anaphases, or diplotene and anaphase II.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a dividing cell of a diploid organism, a group of chromosomes has reached each pole, the nuclear membrane and nucleolus are reappearing, each group has half the chromosome number of the parent cell, and each chromosome still consists of two chromatids. The cell is in:

options.text: the concentration of CO2 in the atmosphere
the genetic predisposition and the growth of the plant

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Plants in which the first product of CO2 fixation is a C4 acid, oxaloacetic acid (OAA), are said to follow the:

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): During the light reaction, the pH in the lumen of the thylakoid decreases.
Reason (R): Protons accumulate in the lumen, both from the splitting of water and from the H carrier that releases into the lumen the protons it removed from the stroma.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

solution.explanation: The splitting of water occurs on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane, so its protons accumulate in the lumen.
